simple.meaning: סֹבֶא (çôbeʼ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “potation , concretely ( wine ), or abstractly ( carousal ).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Deuteronomy, Isaiah, Hosea, Nahum, beginning at Deuteronomy 21:20. The surrounding contexts include birth, family line, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סֹבֶא (H5435) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: סֹבֶא (çôbeʼ) / H5435 is traced through Deuteronomy 21:20, Isaiah 1:22, Hosea 4:18, Nahum 1:10 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H5435. sobe [ סֹ֫בֶא ] noun masculine Isa 1:22 drink, liquor ; — only suffix סָבְאֵךְ 1:22 ; סָבְאָם Hosea 4:18 (but see below), Nahum 1:10 (but see סָבָא ); — liquor (apparently strong, choice) Isa 1:22 ; ס ׳סָר Hosea 4:18 their liquor (i.e. their drunkenness) is gone Thes Hi Che RVm, but very dubious, ᵐ5 quite different ( ἡρέτισεν Χαναναίους ), We Gu Kau Now omit in translation; conjecture of Houtsma TTijdschr ix (1875), 60 סֹבְאִים סֹד , a company of wine-bibbers , makes good sense.

occurrences.englishText: They shall tell the elders of his city, “This our son is stubborn and rebellious. He will not obey our voice. He is a glutton and a drunkard.”
For entangled like thorns, and drunken as with their drink, they are consumed utterly like dry stubble.
